stories.title: AG Poly Packs folds its Gujarat subsidiary into the parent
stories.summary: AG Poly Packs, a rigid plastic packaging maker with consolidated revenue of about ₹300 crore in FY2025-26, is merging its wholly owned subsidiary AG Petuela into itself. The Umbergaon unit's annual revenue has grown from about ₹18 crore at acquisition in September 2024 to about ₹48 crore.

stories.title: Supreme Industries grows H1 revenue 22 per cent as piping volumes jump
stories.summary: Supreme Industries reported standalone H1 FY27 revenue from operations of ₹6,079 crore, up from ₹5,003 crore, on sales volume of 341,991 tonnes, according to its earnings call transcript. Operating profit rose 34 per cent to ₹829 crore and profit after tax grew 31 per cent to ₹487 crore.

stories.title: Apt Packaging's profit rises 366 per cent, with an auditor's footnote
stories.summary: Apt Packaging reported Q2 FY27 net profit of ₹211.78 lakh, up 366 per cent from ₹45.43 lakh, as revenue more than doubled to ₹1,308.15 lakh. Trade receivables rose to ₹1,277.44 lakh, and the auditor qualified the results over ₹11.45 lakh of unprovisioned doubtful debts.

stories.title: EPL's Hariharan K. Nair on making tubes recyclable without losing the product
stories.summary: EPL says the packaging challenge is now recycling without compromising protection, looks or commercial viability. The tube maker is pursuing this through recyclable tube formats, more post-consumer recycled material and material efficiency, with platforms such as Platina, the company says. The tube is being asked to do a lot.

stories.title: Ahmedabad seals 20 units and seizes 23kg of banned plastic
stories.summary: Ahmedabad's civic body inspected 239 units in its West Zone during a three-night drive from 28 to 30 October, issuing notices to 153. Officials seized 23kg of banned plastic, sealed 20 units for littering in public places and collected Rs 2.6 lakh in fines.

stories.title: Milk packets, chips wrappers and paper bags, sorted by what India can recycle
stories.summary: A Times of India explainer looks at which everyday packaging can realistically be recycled within India's waste system. EcoEx co-founder Akshaya Rath says technology can strengthen extended producer responsibility compliance for producers, importers and brand owners. The piece argues collection, segregation and certified recyclers matter as much as awareness.

stories.title: Hormel splits its bacon pack for people who only want two slices
stories.summary: Hormel has introduced Black Label Portion Pack Bacon, with smaller pre-portioned sections so buyers can open only the amount they need. Sporked says the format solves the problem of the rest of the pack waiting in the fridge after a breakfast for one. Bacon, at last, respects boundaries.

stories.title: FOLI's interlocking oil bottles go viral on purpose
stories.summary: FOLI's interlocking bottles for its high-end oils and dressings have been going viral on social media over recent months, Packaging Europe reports. The bottles are designed to encourage interaction, reuse and collectability to stand out in a crowded category. The full interview with founder Nohra Currie is for subscribers.

stories.title: Opackgroup puts a 50 per cent recycled sleeve on a recycled PET bottle
stories.summary: OPACKGROUP and recycler Morssinkhof-Rymoplast have applied a stretch sleeve made from at least 50 per cent post-consumer recycled material to a recycled PET bottle and cap. The sleeve goes on without adhesive, which the companies say improves separability and recyclability while keeping shelf appeal.

stories.title: Plastic mesh tea bags can add thousands of microplastics per cup, study finds
stories.summary: Researchers at Recep Tayyip Erdogan University in Türkiye found that tea brewed from plastic-mesh tea bags used by some brands carried between 555 and 2,498 microplastic particles per cup on average, Gizmodo reports. They also detected concerning amounts of BPA and similar endocrine-disrupting chemicals.

stories.title: Eggs and honey turn up in a review of microplastics in food
stories.summary: Ultra-processed foods such as instant ramen are known sources of microplastic shedding, but a new scientific review suggests whole foods like eggs and honey are not spared either, AOL reports. Food is a major route because of all the plastic it touches before it reaches the table.

stories.title: Microplastics fall with the snow at every Sierra Nevada site sampled
stories.summary: Scientists measuring microplastic deposition across the Sierra Nevada during snowstorms found plastic particles at every site they sampled, including remote spots reachable only by chairlift or on skis. The snowpack supplies roughly 30 per cent of California's freshwater, raising questions about contamination downstream.

stories.title: Microplastics are raining on Everest all year, Chinese researchers say
stories.summary: A study by Chinese researchers found microplastic and nanoplastic particles reaching Mount Everest year-round through atmospheric circulation, The Independent reports. The Tibetan Plateau could be accumulating an estimated 56 tonnes of airborne microplastics a year at altitudes above 4,000 metres.

stories.title: Why black plastic bags should not touch food
stories.summary: JurnalPost looks at the common practice of wrapping food in black plastic bags in local culinary trade. It argues food safety depends on packaging as much as clean ingredients, and that materials not meant for food contact can pose health risks when food sits directly against them.

stories.title: PTT and Siam Cement will combine their polyolefin units
stories.summary: Thailand's PTT Group and Siam Cement Group will set up a joint venture to make commodity-grade plastics, the companies announced on Thursday, Nikkei Asia reports. They say the venture will rank among the world's top 10 producers and be one of Southeast Asia's largest in the sector.

stories.title: Myers Industries falls 6 per cent after a resin cost spike
stories.summary: Myers Industries closed down about 6 per cent after third-quarter revenue rose 8.1 per cent but gross margin fell to 27.3 per cent, TIKR reports. Price increases have not caught up with resin costs. Higher polyethylene prices lifted Dow's plastics profits. One company's cost is another's margin.

stories.title: Petkim picks Univation technology for an 850,000 tonne polyethylene complex
stories.summary: Türkiye's Petkim has selected Univation's UNIPOL PE process for a planned polyethylene complex at Aliaga-Izmir, ahead of its final investment decision. The project would have 850,000 tonnes a year of licensed resin capacity across two 425,000 tonne reactor lines.

stories.title: Ganesha Ecosphere swings to a ₹28.1 crore quarterly profit
stories.summary: PET recycler Ganesha Ecosphere reported Q2 consolidated net profit of ₹28.1 crore against a loss of ₹50 lakh a year earlier. Revenue rose to ₹513 crore on strong volumes across recycling operations, and EBITDA reached ₹60.6 crore with a margin of 11.82 per cent.

stories.title: NGT pulls up Bhopal over illegal plastic recycling units
stories.summary: The National Green Tribunal has pulled up the Bhopal Municipal Corporation for failing to detail action against illegal plastic recycling units, enforcement of the single-use plastic ban and e-waste disposal. The tribunal said the compliance report fell short and directed the corporation to file a detailed response.

stories.title: Danone will rewrite recycling claims on its bottles across Europe
stories.summary: Danone has agreed to change recycling-related claims on its plastic bottles across Europe after talks with EU consumer protection authorities, coordinated by the Swedish Consumer Agency and the Hungarian Competition Authority. It has 18 months to revise bottle labels and three months to update digital marketing.

stories.title: Colorado's recycling programme grows, along with its lawsuits
stories.summary: Colorado's statewide recycling programme is starting to seed free collection in several cities, but it faces two lawsuits filed in the past seven months. A debate over whether chemical recycling of harder-to-recycle items should count as recycling continues. An advisory board discussed it last year and took no action.

stories.title: BIR says plastic recycling is under growing pressure
stories.summary: Weak demand, high costs and uncertain EU regulations are putting pressure on plastic recycling, according to RECYCLING magazin. The Bureau of International Recycling is calling for fair competition and reliable rules.

stories.title: UK deposit return scheme publishes its first list of certified machines
stories.summary: Exchange for Change, which runs the UK's upcoming deposit return scheme, has published its first list of certified reverse vending machines. Each machine was tested against 77 requirements by an independent assessor. The list is meant to help retailers prepare for the scheme's launch next year.

stories.title: Councils in England get a list of recycling they need not collect
stories.summary: The UK government has listed several common household items, including types of glass, metals, plastic and card, that English councils are not obliged to collect for recycling, The Mirror reports. A rule due to start from March 2027 has also been pushed back three years.

stories.title: An Australian bin crushes soft plastics at the supermarket
stories.summary: An Australian company's plastic-crushing bin has been trialled at six supermarkets overseas and is being pitched as 'the future' of soft plastics recycling, Yahoo News reports. Most soft plastics end up in landfill. Aussie shoppers can currently only drop them at Woolworths stores.

stories.title: Republic Services gets $16 more a ton for recyclables
stories.summary: Waste and recycling company Republic Services says it received an average of $16 per ton more for recycled commodities this summer than in July to September 2025, as it reported a year-on-year income boost.

stories.title: Weight-loss jab needles are turning up at Coventry's recycling plant
stories.summary: The boom in injectable weight-loss drugs such as Mounjaro and Wegovy is sending more used needles to recycling centres, putting workers at risk of injury and infection, bosses told the BBC. At a Coventry plant, a crushed sharps container appeared on the sorting conveyor during the visit.

stories.title: Chemically recycled ABS is tested for hospital 3D printing
stories.summary: A study in Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology examines whether chemically recycled ABS plastic can be used to 3D print medical devices such as surgical guides and anatomical models. Researchers want to know if recycled material can meet the precision and safety needs of hospital use.

stories.title: Panchkula orders strict enforcement of the 2026 waste rules
stories.summary: Panchkula Deputy Commissioner Satpal Sharma has directed departments to strictly implement the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, against illegal dumping, transport and disposal. Orders include segregation at source, mapping of bulk waste generators, covered garbage vehicles and regular cleaning of vulnerable points, with compliance due at the next review.

stories.title: Sikkim High Court orders statewide inspections over waste disposal
stories.summary: The Sikkim High Court has directed the pollution control board, district administrations and legal services authorities to jointly inspect pharmaceutical companies and other industries over waste on farmland and untreated effluents. The government must frame sewerage rules within three months. Hotels without board consent must shut after 31 March 2027.

stories.title: UK review finds plastic packaging tax cut taxable material by a fifth
stories.summary: A UK government analysis of the Plastic Packaging Tax, charged on packaging with under 30 per cent recycled plastic, found taxable material placed on the market fell by a fifth in 2025/26. It found 'limited evidence of widespread behavioural change' beyond a subset of businesses.

stories.title: The Grocer says the UK packaging regime survives every complaint
stories.summary: Retailers and manufacturers have long called the UK's packaging regime outdated and costly, The Grocer writes. PRN prices have in some cases more than trebled since January. The BRC's Tom Ironside says overlapping packaging taxes cost the industry billions. The column argues the barrier to reform is not technical.

stories.title: Foodservice packaging body wants recycled-content certification kept practical
stories.summary: The Foodservice Packaging Association welcomed Budget support for energy-intensive manufacturing but warned of regulatory pressure on packaging supply chains. Mandatory certification of mechanically recycled plastic for Plastic Packaging Tax purposes will come in from April 2030. The FPA says certification must be practical and proportionate.

stories.title: Wales bans wet wipes containing plastic from 18 December
stories.summary: Supplying wet wipes containing plastic to consumers in Wales becomes an offence from 18 December, including in shops, online and when free. The ban covers baby wipes, make-up wipes, moist toilet tissue, antibacterial and cleaning wipes. Reusable and plastic-free alternatives are not affected.

stories.title: Call to pause Wales's 20p deposit return scheme
stories.summary: Clwyd MS Louise Emery has asked the Welsh Government to pause its deposit return scheme, saying the 20p charge could hit vulnerable families, the elderly and the disabled hardest. Launching on 1 October 2027, it covers PET, cans and glass. Wales is the only UK nation including glass.

stories.title: Nepal's lawmakers file 212 amendments to the waste management bill
stories.summary: Lawmakers in Nepal have registered 212 amendment notices to the Solid Waste Management Bill, 2083, seeking to shift it from a disposal model to a source-based circular economy model built on human rights. The Speaker has approved clause-by-clause discussion of the bill in the House.

stories.title: Contract packers say the Budget overlooked them
stories.summary: The BCMPA, representing contract manufacturers, packers, fulfilment and logistics firms, says the UK Budget failed to address the combined impact of employment costs, energy prices and regulation on small and medium businesses. Chief executive Emma Verkaik said the Budget 'overlooks many of the businesses' delivering growth.

stories.title: Kerala Paper Products gets approval for ₹741 crore expansion
stories.summary: State-owned Kerala Paper Products Limited, the only paper maker in Kerala, has received government approval for projects worth ₹741 crore to make products beyond newsprint. A bank-appointed agency gave a favourable feasibility report. The state will put in ₹200 crore as equity, with a banking consortium funding the rest.

stories.title: Emami Paper's quarterly profit rises to ₹44.43 crore from ₹6.58 crore
stories.summary: Emami Paper Mills reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of ₹589.78 crore, up from ₹450.61 crore a year earlier. Profit after tax rose to ₹44.43 crore from ₹6.58 crore. The board also approved a re-appointment, according to its filing.

stories.title: Pakka posts Q2 profit, with a qualified review on an overseas project
stories.summary: Pakka reported standalone Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹12,404.39 lakh and profit after tax of ₹288.28 lakh. The consolidated review carries a qualified conclusion over ₹3,247.23 lakh of capital work in progress at an overseas subsidiary whose project resumption remains uncertain.

stories.title: Pudumjee Paper grows half-year turnover to ₹430 crore
stories.summary: Pudumjee Paper Products reported H1 FY27 turnover of ₹430 crore, up from ₹404 crore, with EBITDA of ₹90 crore or 21 per cent of turnover. Tonnage rose about 2 per cent and realisations about 4 per cent, partly offsetting raw material costs. It is seeking clearance for a Mahad project.

stories.title: Saica opens a €100 million corrugated plant near Barcelona
stories.summary: Saica Group has opened its new Saica Pack corrugated packaging plant in Sant Esteve Sesrovires, Barcelona, after investing more than €100 million. Fully running three years after the foundation stone was laid, it has capacity of 200 million square metres and merges two older Barcelona area sites.

stories.title: Georgia-Pacific spends $150 million replacing a 1980 paper machine
stories.summary: Georgia-Pacific is investing about $150 million to rebuild a paper machine at its Palatka, Florida, mill, replacing the Number Four machine installed in 1980. The project supports its consumer tissue business. Work has begun and is due to finish in the second quarter of 2028.

stories.title: MM Kwidzyn's new digester cuts CO2 by about a third
stories.summary: MM Board & Paper has completed a continuous cooking investment at MM Kwidzyn in Poland, which makes cartonboard, packaging kraft paper and pulp. The new digester should cut the mill's CO2 emissions by around a third and wood use by about 50,000 cubic metres a year.

stories.title: Paper bottles head to Italy by late 2027
stories.summary: Swiss manufacturer Perlen Papier will launch paper-fibre bottles developed by British firm Pulpex in Italy towards the end of 2027. Pulpex recently opened its first plant in Glasgow with annual capacity of 40 to 50 million units. Perlen has an exclusive partnership with it since April.

stories.title: Innocent tests a swallowable drink pod in a village called Nobottle
stories.summary: Innocent drinks and Notpla have piloted a seaweed-based Ooho pod that can be popped into the mouth and swallowed, replacing the bottle. The trial took place in Nobottle, a Northamptonshire hamlet of around 30 people, whose residents were the first to try it. Someone in marketing had a good week.

stories.title: Redysign builds wood-based pads for fresh meat trays
stories.summary: The EU-backed Redysign project reports advances on a wood-based absorbent pad for fresh meat packaging. Conventional pads rely on synthetic materials and adhesives that contaminate paper waste streams and can make the whole pack unrecyclable. The project aims to remove that last stubborn bit of plastic.

stories.title: Valcolatte wraps its burrata in recyclable paper
stories.summary: Italian dairy producer Caseificio Valcolatte has introduced its first recyclable paper packaging, starting with its signature burrata, Food and Drink Technology reports. The company makes traditional cheeses from 100 per cent Italian milk and says the move aligns that heritage with modern ecological expectations.

stories.title: O-I Glass cuts its outlook as European demand weakens
stories.summary: O-I Glass lowered its 2026 earnings outlook after third-quarter net sales fell 2 per cent to $1.62 billion. Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $234 million from $329 million. European revenue fell about 8 per cent to $634 million, and European segment profit slid to $2 million from $95 million.

stories.title: Croxsons measures carbon across the glass bottle supply chain
stories.summary: Croxsons, a fifth-generation family glass packaging supplier and B Corp, uses Greenly to measure emissions across Scopes 1, 2 and 3. It says the question is not only its own operations but the impact of the products it brings to market. Glass is infinitely recyclable and energy hungry to make.

stories.title: Biodegradable films are promising and still weaker than plastic, review finds
stories.summary: A review in Discover Chemical Engineering led by Sakshi Singh pulls together evidence on biodegradable packaging films, covering strength, barrier behaviour, food uses and safety. Tensile strength across the studies ranged from about 0.7 to 32 megapascals. The authors find the films remain no match for plastics yet.

stories.title: Oak Ridge launches a national effort to modernise the paper industry
stories.summary: Oak Ridge National Laboratory has launched CRAFT, the Center for Research and Advancement of Forest Product Technologies, bringing national labs, universities and industry together to develop technology for US pulp, paper and packaging. National director Dan Coughlin said it is critical to rural communities that rely on paper mills.

stories.title: Akshar NX Digital adds a larger Flexcel platemaker for flexible packaging
stories.summary: Ahmedabad prepress specialist Akshar NX Digital has invested in a Miraclon Flexcel NX 5080 system to serve flexible packaging, due for installation in January 2027 at a new location. It joins the Flexcel NX 4260 already running in Ahmedabad, along with new colour management investment.

stories.title: Ankit Graphics buys Esko Quartz for wide-web flexo plates
stories.summary: Ahmedabad flexo prepress shop Ankit Graphics, in plate-making since 1987, has invested in Esko CDI Crystal Quartz in the 4260 format to expand into wide-web flexible packaging. Ankit Darji said the decision followed months of evaluation, including a visit to Germany to understand the technology.

stories.title: BW Packaging launches a washdown flow wrapper for cheese
stories.summary: BW Packaging, Barry-Wehmiller's packaging machinery business, has launched the Hayssen X650 flow wrapper for cheese and other hygiene-sensitive foods. It combines hermetic sealing and full washdown construction with speeds up to 150 packs a minute, plus jam detection, RFID login and recipe-driven settings.

stories.title: UNTHA's new shredder targets plastics that refuse to be shredded
stories.summary: UNTHA has launched the MR1800C PRO universal shredder, designed to process thick-walled sprues, moulded parts, pipes, film bales and composites without pretreatment. Its beltless power drive removes typical sources of wear. It is aimed at plastic processors, recyclers and multi-shift industrial sites.

stories.title: Ranpak reaches operating breakeven while carrying a $402.8 million loan
stories.summary: Ranpak reported third-quarter revenue of $101.9 million with improved gross margin and an operating breakeven, as it shifts towards higher-margin automation equipment and away from commodity protective packaging, Alpha Spread writes. A $402.8 million term loan continues to suppress bottom-line profitability.

stories.title: Digital printing puts your name on the yoghurt lid
stories.summary: Digital printing lets brands run Christmas editions, personalised messages and promotions on lids without conventional printing's limits, Sustainable Packaging News writes. Multiple designs, small runs, tight deadlines and late changes are hard for conventional processes. The yoghurt now knows who you are.

stories.title: Flint Group says coatings are no longer an afterthought
stories.summary: Flint Group Packaging Solutions has published a whitepaper, Beyond the Surface, arguing coatings have moved from a finishing step to a strategic part of packaging design. It examines how coatings shape how packaging looks, performs and is recovered at end of life. Flint Group sells coatings.

stories.title: Prataap Snacks grows income 26 per cent and slips to a loss
stories.summary: Prataap Snacks reported Q2 FY27 income from operations of ₹540.95 crore, up 25.9 per cent. Operating EBITDA fell to ₹12.9 crore from ₹22.9 crore, and it posted a net loss of ₹2.5 crore against a ₹4.64 crore profit a year earlier. It plans a new Indore facility.

stories.title: Milky Mist's quarterly profit grows 174.5 per cent
stories.summary: Milky Mist Dairy Food, which calls itself India's fastest-growing packaged food company, reported Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹1,089.40 crore, up 41.58 per cent from ₹769.47 crore. EBITDA rose 53.90 per cent to ₹165.21 crore and the company reported 174.5 per cent profit growth.

stories.title: Dodla Dairy's revenue rises as milk costs squeeze profit
stories.summary: Dodla Dairy reported higher Q2 FY27 revenue on record milk procurement and growing curd volumes, while profit after tax declined as raw milk costs climbed faster than realisations. Its African business grew, and a greenfield Maharashtra plant is due to start commercial operations by the end of FY27.

stories.title: Sunrise Foods fined ₹1 lakh over '100% whole wheat' bread that was 64%
stories.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority has fined Sunrise Foods ₹1 lakh for its 'Everyday 100% Whole Wheat Bread' packaging after finding the product contained only 64 per cent whole wheat. The pack, as ever, was more confident than the loaf.

stories.title: HUL backs FSSAI front-of-pack warning labels
stories.summary: Hindustan Unilever has publicly supported FSSAI's food labelling norms, under which packaged foods high in saturated fat, sugar and salt will carry prominent front-of-pack warnings, OC Academy reports. Healthcare professionals have welcomed the stance, saying clear disclosures help patients make informed choices.

stories.title: Festive FMCG demand is won with the pack, not the discount
stories.summary: In FMCG, the festive lever is a pack that fits the occasion rather than a bigger discount, an Indian Retailer column argues. It describes a smaller festive pack of eight or ten bottles, light enough for a family visit, beside the 24 bottle case. Nobody cut the price, it notes.

stories.title: HUL, ITC, Dabur and Britannia fall up to 46 per cent in a year
stories.summary: Several established FMCG companies including HUL, ITC, Dabur and Britannia have fallen by up to 46 per cent in a year amid worries about earnings growth, higher raw material prices and valuations. The piece says the main task for companies is now driving profitability.

stories.title: Goyal asks FMCG companies to spread ONDC's DigiDukaan to kiranas
stories.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal has urged FMCG companies to expand ONDC's DigiDukaan initiative, digitising kirana procurement to improve transparency and free up working capital. He chaired a roundtable with over 40 industry leaders under the Bharat Commerce Chintan Shivir, according to a ministry release.

stories.title: Cheerios gets a resealable Ziploc bag inside the box
stories.summary: General Mills is packing Cheerios in a resealable Ziploc bag inside the existing box, with a partial top opening for a pour spot. It says 90 per cent of consumers already fold, roll, clip or decant their cereal to keep it fresh. The clip industry has been notified.

stories.title: Jägermeister trims packaging weight on its travel retail gift packs
stories.summary: Mast-Jägermeister has launched new travel retail-exclusive gift packs focused on cutting packaging material and weight: a Twin Pack, a Shot Cup Pack and a Party Pack with ten aluminium shot cups. The boxes have tactile embossing and a braided handle, and printing has been optimised for recyclability.

stories.title: Stora Enso's board approves spinning off its Swedish forests
stories.summary: Stora Enso's board has approved spinning off its Swedish forest assets into a separately listed company, Bergslagets Skogar, expected in March 2027 subject to shareholder approval. It would be what Stora Enso calls Europe's largest listed pure-play forest company, leaving the group focused on packaging and renewable materials.

stories.title: UFlex shareholders approve borrowing of up to ₹5,000 crore
stories.summary: UFlex shareholders have passed a special resolution through postal ballot letting the board borrow up to ₹5,000 crore under Section 180(1)(c) of the Companies Act. The result was filed on 31 October, with 99.92 per cent of valid votes cast in favour.

stories.title: Odisha clears ₹3,855 crore of proposals including paper and packaging
stories.summary: The Odisha government has approved 22 investment proposals worth ₹3,855.38 crore across 12 districts, expected to create 7,765 jobs. The projects span aerospace and defence, compressed biogas, pharmaceuticals, paper and packaging, manufacturing and hospitality, as the state widens beyond metals and mining.

stories.title: Vedant Poly Fabs lifts margins by dropping trading for manufacturing
stories.summary: Vedant Poly Fabs raised its FY26 profit after tax margin to 9.52 per cent from 5.63 per cent by shifting to flexible packaging manufacturing, which made up 96.37 per cent of revenue against 62.75 per cent a year earlier. Manufacturing revenue rose 118.23 per cent to ₹110.96 crore.

stories.title: Dosiujeun signs a $18.7 million plastic recycling equipment deal
stories.summary: South Korea's Dosiujeun has signed a 25 billion won contract with PlasticX to supply its RGO waste-plastic recycled material production units, totalling 50 tons in capacity, for domestic recyclers by 2027. The company is eyeing expansion into Indonesia, Vietnam and other markets.

stories.title: UFP Industries buys Apache Products on the Gulf Coast
stories.summary: UFP Industries has acquired Texas-based Apache Products, expanding its packaging division along the Gulf Coast. The deal adds facilities serving industrial and petrochemical customers across the Texas and Louisiana corridor, one of the largest US petrochemical hubs.

events.line: Enterprise Ireland webinar with Repak on PPWR producer duties, reporting and Ireland's EPR transition.
